questions.question:
Which number will replace the question mark (?) in the following series?

105, 106, 114, 141, ?
questions.solution:
The logic is:

105 + 1³ = 106

106 + 2³ = 114

114 + 3³ = 141

141 + 4³ = 205

Hence, ‘205’ is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number.

12 : 121 : : 10 : ?
questions.solution:
The logic is:

12 : 121 → 12 : (12 – 1)²

Similarly,

10 : ? → 10 : (10 – 1)²

? = 9² = 81

Hence, 81 is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the word pair in which the two words are related in the same way as the two words in the following word-pair.

Skin : Eczema
questions.solution:
The logic is:

Skin : Eczema → Eczema is a condition where patches of skin become inflamed, itchy, red, cracked, and rough.

Or, we can say that Eczema is a disease of the skin. (Organ – Disease)

Similarly,

1) Heart : Blood → Not a pair of (Organ – Disease)

2) Lungs : Oxygen → Not a pair of (Organ – Disease)

3) Eyes : Cataract → Pair of (Organ – Disease)

4) Kidney : Diabetes → Not a pair of (Organ – Disease)

Hence, ‘Eyes : Cataract’ is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Two statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some caps are shirts.

Some shirts are coats.

**Conclusions:**

I. No coat is cap.

II. No coat is shirt.

III. Some coats are caps

options.text: Either conclusion I or III follow.
Either conclusion II or III follow.

questions.solution:
__Concept:__

 
• The *neither-nor* case is applicable when both the conclusions are false, whether definite or not.
 
• The *either-or* case is applicable for a pair of statements *only if* either of the following pair of *keywords* is used AND *only if* the following *conditions* are satisfied:

Keywords:

 
• *All* and *some not*
 
• *Some* and *no*

Conditions:

 
• The *same elements* are used in the two conclusions. For example, in this case, the elements *jungles* and *malls* are common to both conclusions.
 
• Both conclusions should be possibilities. That is, they should be *false because the conclusion is possible but not definite*.

Then, the pair of conclusions are considered as *complementary pairs.*

The least possible venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dc9db11ccac2366777c3c95fbe1bd1c2030beb759b17bc4cf119eedf0a5fbd90.png] 

I. No coat is cap. → False (There is no direct relation given between caps and coats so it can be possible but not definite, hence false)

II. No coat is shirt. → False (as some shirts are coats given so some coats can be shirts it is definite, but no coat is shirt, it is not possible)

III. Some coats are caps. → False (there is no direct relation given between caps and coats so it can be possible but not definite, hence false)

But, I and III forms a complementary pair.

Hence, **either conclusion I or III follows.**

questions.question:
Which two signs and two numbers should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

28 + 4 × 16 ÷ 5 – 17 = 127
questions.solution:
1) 4 and 5, + and ×

Given equation: 28 + 4 × 16 ÷ 5 – 17 = 127

After interchanging ‘4 and 5, + and ×’, we get:

L.H.S = 28 × 5 + 16 ÷ 4 – 17

= 140 + 4 – 17

= 144 – 17

= 127 = R.H.S

2) 28 and 16, + and ÷

Given equation: 28 + 4 × 16 ÷ 5 – 17 = 127

After interchanging ‘28 and 16, + and ÷’, we get:

L.H.S = 16 ÷ 4 × 28 + 5 – 17

= 112 + 5 – 17

= 117 – 17

= 100 ≠ R.H.S

3) 4 and 5, + and –

Given equation: 28 + 4 × 16 ÷ 5 – 17 = 127

After interchanging ‘4 and 5, + and –’, we get:

L.H.S = 28 - 5 × 16 ÷ 4 + 17

= 28 - 20 + 17

= 45 – 20

= 25 ≠ R.H.S

4) 28 and 5, ÷ and ×

Given equation: 28 + 4 × 16 ÷ 5 – 17 = 127

After interchanging ‘28 and 5, ÷ and ×’, we get:

L.H.S = 5 + 4 ÷ 16 × 28 – 17

= 5 + 7 – 17

= 12 – 17

= - 5 ≠ R.H.S

Hence, ‘4 and 5, + and ×’ is the correct answer

questions.question: Amrit is elder than Vikrant. Shanaz is elder than Joya. Ketan is younger than Joya.Vikrant is elder than Shanaz. Who is the youngest in the group?
questions.solution:
1. Amrit is elder than Vikrant.

Amrit > Vikrant

2. Shanaz is elder than Joya.

Shanaz > Joya

3. Ketan is younger than Joya.

Joya > Ketan

4. Vikrant is elder than Shanaz.

Vikrant > Shanaz

Combining all the statements together,

we get:

Amrit > Vikrant > Shanaz > Joya > Ketan

Hence, Ketan is the youngest in the group.
